• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar → Chairman of Drafting Committee.

PYQ Trap
• Ambedkar = Chairman of Drafting Committee (very important).

COMMITTEES OF CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY

Important Points
• Drafting Committee – B.R. Ambedkar
• Union Constitution Committee – Jawaharlal Nehru
• Fundamental Rights Committee – Sardar Patel

PYQ Trap
• Patel handled Fundamental Rights and Minorities committees.

DRAFTING OF CONSTITUTION

Features
• Drafting Committee formed in 1947.
• Draft Constitution prepared by B.N. Rau (Constitutional Advisor).

Important Points
• Final draft adopted on 26 November 1949.
• Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.

PYQ Trap
• 26 November → Adoption, 26 January → Enforcement.

TIME TAKEN

Important Points
• Took 2 years, 11 months, 18 days.

COST OF CONSTITUTION

Important Points
• Approx. ₹64 lakh spent.

SOURCES OF CONSTITUTION

Features
• Borrowed from multiple countries.

Important Points
• UK → Parliamentary system
• USA → Fundamental Rights
• Ireland → DPSP
• Canada → Federal system with strong centre

PYQ Trap
• Borrowed features frequently asked.

SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS OF ASSEMBLY

Important Points
• Representative body.
• Included leaders from different backgrounds.
• Debates ensured detailed discussion.

CRITICISM

Important Points
• Not directly elected by people.
• Dominated by Congress.

Significance
• Provided democratic foundation.
• Reflected diversity of India.
• Ensured rights and governance structure.

Conclusion
• The Constituent Assembly successfully framed a comprehensive Constitution.
• It laid the foundation for democratic governance in independent India.
Polity.Salient Features of the Indian Constitut:
SALIENT FEATURES OF THE INDIAN CONSTITUTION

Introduction
• The Indian Constitution is a unique document combining features from various constitutions of the world.
• It establishes a sovereign, democratic framework for governance.

Important Points
• Longest written Constitution in the world.
• Blend of rigidity and flexibility.

PYQ Trap
• Indian Constitution is neither fully rigid nor fully flexible.

WRITTEN AND DETAILED CONSTITUTION

Features
• Contains detailed provisions regarding governance.
• Originally had 395 Articles and 8 Schedules.

PYQ Trap
• Presently → 450+ Articles and 12 Schedules.

SOVEREIGN STATE

Features
• India is independent in internal and external matters.

SOCIALIST AND SECULAR STATE

Features
• Added by 42nd Amendment (1976).
• Ensures equality and religious neutrality.

PYQ Trap
• Socialist and Secular added later, not original.

DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC

Features
• Government elected by people.
• President is elected (not hereditary).

PARLIAMENTARY SYSTEM

Features
• Executive responsible to legislature.
• Prime Minister is real executive.

PYQ Trap
• Parliamentary system borrowed from UK.

FEDERAL SYSTEM WITH UNITARY BIAS

Features
• Division of powers between Centre and States.
• Strong central government.

PYQ Trap
• India is federal but with unitary features.

INTEGRATED JUDICIARY

Features
• Single unified judicial system.
• Supreme Court at top.

FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS

Features
• Guarantee civil liberties.
• Justiciable in courts.

PYQ Trap
• Enforceable by courts (key point).

DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY

Features
• Guidelines for state policy.
• Non-justiciable.

PYQ Trap
• DPSP not enforceable in courts.

FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES

Features
• Added by 42nd Amendment.

UNIVERSAL ADULT FRANCHISE

Features
• All citizens above 18 years can vote.

PYQ Trap
• Voting age reduced from 21 to 18 by 61st Amendment.

INDEPENDENT JUDICIARY

Features
• Judiciary free from executive interference.

EMERGENCY PROVISIONS

Features
• Centre gets more power during emergencies.

PYQ Trap
• Emergency provisions borrowed from Germany.

SINGLE CITIZENSHIP

Features
• Only one citizenship for entire country.

PYQ Trap
• Unlike USA, India has single citizenship.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures stability and flexibility.
• Maintains unity in diversity.
• Protects rights and governance structure.

Conclusion
• The Indian Constitution is a balanced document combining global ideas with Indian needs.
• It forms the backbone of democratic governance in India.
Polity.Preamble:
PREAMBLE OF THE INDIAN CONSTITUTION

Introduction
• The Preamble is the introductory statement of the Constitution which sets out the philosophy and objectives of the Constitution.
• It reflects the ideals and aspirations of the people of India.

Important Points
• Based on the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1946.

PYQ Trap
• Preamble is based on Objectives Resolution.

KEY WORDS IN PREAMBLE

Features
• Sovereign – India is independent internally and externally.
• Socialist – Promotes social and economic equality.
• Secular – Equal respect to all religions.
• Democratic – Government elected by people.
• Republic – Head of state is elected.

PYQ Trap
• Socialist and Secular added by 42nd Amendment (1976).

OBJECTIVES OF PREAMBLE

Features
• Justice – Social, Economic and Political.
• Liberty – Thought, expression, belief, faith and worship.
• Equality – Status and opportunity.
• Fraternity – Unity and integrity of the nation.

PYQ Trap
• Fraternity ensures dignity of individual and unity of nation.

NATURE OF PREAMBLE

Important Points
• Not a source of power.
• Acts as guiding principle for interpretation.

PYQ Trap
• Preamble is not enforceable in court.

AMENDABILITY OF PREAMBLE

Important Points
• Preamble can be amended under Article 368.

PYQ Trap
• Kesavananda Bharati case → Preamble is part of Constitution.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Reflects core philosophy of Constitution.
• Helps in interpretation of constitutional provisions.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• Berubari Case (1960) → Preamble not part of Constitution (initial view).
• Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973) → Preamble is part of Constitution.

PYQ Trap
• Kesavananda reversed Berubari.

CONCLUSION

Conclusion
• The Preamble is the soul of the Constitution.
• It guides the functioning of the Indian political system.
Polity.Citizenship:
CITIZENSHIP

Introduction
• Citizenship denotes the legal relationship between an individual and the State.
• It provides rights, duties and political identity to a person.

Important Points
• Articles 5 to 11 deal with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.

PYQ Trap
• Citizenship provisions in Constitution are temporary in nature.

CONSTITUTIONAL PROVISIONS

Features
• Article 5 – Citizenship at commencement.
• Article 6 – Citizenship for migrants from Pakistan.
• Article 7 – Citizenship for migrants to Pakistan.
• Article 8 – Citizenship for persons of Indian origin abroad.
• Article 9 – No dual citizenship.
• Article 10 – Continuance of citizenship.
• Article 11 – Parliament’s power to regulate citizenship.

PYQ Trap
• Parliament has power to regulate citizenship under Article 11.

CITIZENSHIP ACT 1955

Features
• Provides detailed provisions for acquisition and loss of citizenship.

MODES OF ACQUIRING CITIZENSHIP

Features
• By Birth
• By Descent
• By Registration
• By Naturalization
• By Incorporation of Territory

PYQ Trap
• Incorporation of territory is rarely asked but important.

LOSS OF CITIZENSHIP

Features
• By Renunciation
• By Termination
• By Deprivation

PYQ Trap
• Deprivation applies in cases of fraud or disloyalty.

SINGLE CITIZENSHIP

Features
• India follows single citizenship for entire country.

PYQ Trap
• Unlike USA → no dual citizenship in India.

OVERSEAS CITIZENSHIP OF INDIA (OCI)

Features
• Introduced by amendment to Citizenship Act.
• Provides multiple entry, lifelong visa.

Important Points
• OCI is not dual citizenship.

PYQ Trap
• OCI holders do not have voting rights.

RIGHTS AVAILABLE TO CITIZENS ONLY

Features
• Article 15 – Prohibition of discrimination.
• Article 16 – Equality in public employment.
• Article 19 – Freedom rights.

PYQ Trap
• Article 19 available only to citizens.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Defines membership of State.
• Ensures political participation.

Conclusion
• Citizenship is fundamental to the functioning of a democratic State.
• It defines the rights and responsibilities of individuals in India.
Polity.Fundamental Rights:
FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS

Introduction
• Fundamental Rights (FRs) are the cornerstone of political democracy in India.
• They guarantee civil liberties and act as limitations on State power.

Important Points
• Enshrined in Part III (Articles 12–35).
• Inspired largely from the Bill of Rights (USA).

PYQ Trap
• Part III = Fundamental Rights (very frequent question).

FEATURES OF FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS

Features
• Justiciable and enforceable by courts.
• Available against State action (Article 12 defines State).
• Some rights available only to citizens, others to all persons.
• Not absolute – subject to reasonable restrictions.

PYQ Trap
• Article 12 includes Government, Parliament, State Legislature and authorities.

CLASSIFICATION OF FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS

Features
• Right to Equality (Articles 14–18)
• Right to Freedom (Articles 19–22)
• Right against Exploitation (Articles 23–24)
• Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25–28)
• Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29–30)
• Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32)

PYQ Trap
• Right to Property removed from FR by 44th Amendment (1978).

RIGHT TO EQUALITY

Features
• Article 14 → Equality before law + equal protection of laws.
• Article 15 → Prohibition of discrimination.
• Article 16 → Equality in public employment.
• Article 17 → Abolition of untouchability.
• Article 18 → Abolition of titles.

PYQ Trap
• Article 17 is absolute (no exceptions).

RIGHT TO FREEDOM

Features
• Article 19 → Six freedoms (speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession).
• Article 20 → Protection in criminal laws.
• Article 21 → Right to life and personal liberty.
• Article 22 → Protection against arbitrary arrest.

Important Points
• Article 21 expanded through judicial interpretation (Right to privacy, livelihood, dignity).

PYQ Trap
• Article 21 = most dynamic and expansive right.

RIGHT AGAINST EXPLOITATION

Features
• Article 23 → Prohibits trafficking and forced labour.
• Article 24 → Prohibits child labour in hazardous industries.

RIGHT TO FREEDOM OF RELIGION

Features
• Article 25 → Freedom of conscience and religion.
• Article 26 → Manage religious affairs.
• Article 27 → No tax for promotion of religion.
• Article 28 → No religious instruction in State institutions.

PYQ Trap
• Subject to public order, morality and health.

CULTURAL AND EDUCATIONAL RIGHTS

Features
• Article 29 → Protection of culture and language.
• Article 30 → Minority institutions rights.

PYQ Trap
• Applies to minorities (religious and linguistic).

RIGHT TO CONSTITUTIONAL REMEDIES

Features
• Article 32 → Right to approach Supreme Court.
• Provides remedies for enforcement of FRs.

Important Points
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called it the “Heart and Soul of the Constitution”.

WRITS

Features
• Habeas Corpus – produce detained person.
• Mandamus – command public authority.
• Prohibition – stop lower court.
• Certiorari – quash lower court order.
• Quo Warranto – question authority.

PYQ Trap
• Habeas Corpus most frequently asked.

RESTRICTIONS ON FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS

Features
• Reasonable restrictions imposed by State.
• Grounds include security, public order, morality, etc.

PYQ Trap
• Article 19 rights are not absolute.

SUSPENSION OF FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS

Features
• During National Emergency (Article 352).

Important Points
• Article 20 and 21 cannot be suspended (44th Amendment).

PYQ Trap
• Article 19 automatically suspended only during war/emergency.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• Golaknath Case (1967) → FR cannot be amended (initial view).
• Kesavananda Bharati (1973) → Basic Structure doctrine.
• Maneka Gandhi Case (1978) → Expanded Article 21.

PYQ Trap
• Maneka Gandhi case = due process expansion.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures individual liberty.
• Protects against arbitrary State action.
• Strengthens rule of law.

Conclusion
• Fundamental Rights are essential for maintaining democracy and individual dignity.
• They form the backbone of the Indian constitutional framework.
Polity.Directive Principles of State Policy:
DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY

Introduction
• Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are constitutional directives to the State for establishing social and economic democracy.
• They aim to transform India into a welfare state.

Important Points
• Enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36–51).
• Inspired from Irish Constitution.

PYQ Trap
• DPSP borrowed from Ireland.

FEATURES OF DPSP

Features
• Non-justiciable – cannot be enforced by courts.
• Fundamental in governance of the country (Article 37).
• Binding on State morally, not legally.

PYQ Trap
• Article 37 → DPSP not enforceable but fundamental in governance.

CLASSIFICATION OF DPSP

Features
• Socialist Principles
• Gandhian Principles
• Liberal-Intellectual Principles

PYQ Trap
• Classification is not mentioned in Constitution.

SOCIALIST PRINCIPLES

Features
• Article 38 → Promote welfare of people.
• Article 39 → Equal distribution of resources, equal pay.
• Article 41 → Right to work, education and public assistance.
• Article 42 → Just and humane conditions of work.
• Article 43 → Living wage.

PYQ Trap
• Article 39(d) → Equal pay for equal work.

GANDHIAN PRINCIPLES

Features
• Article 40 → Organisation of village panchayats.
• Article 43 → Promotion of cottage industries.
• Article 46 → Promotion of SC/ST welfare.

PYQ Trap
• Panchayati Raj rooted in Article 40.

LIBERAL-INTELLECTUAL PRINCIPLES

Features
• Article 44 → Uniform Civil Code.
• Article 45 → Early childhood care and education.
• Article 48A → Protection of environment.
• Article 50 → Separation of judiciary from executive.

PYQ Trap
• Article 48A added by 42nd Amendment.

RELATION BETWEEN FR AND DPSP

Important Points
• FR → enforceable rights.
• DPSP → non-enforceable goals.
• Both are complementary, not contradictory.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• Champakam Dorairajan (1951) → FR prevail over DPSP.
• Golaknath (1967) → Limited Parliament power over FR.
• Kesavananda Bharati (1973) → Harmony between FR and DPSP.
• Minerva Mills (1980) → Balance between FR and DPSP is part of basic structure.

PYQ Trap
• Minerva Mills → balance between FR and DPSP.

IMPLEMENTATION OF DPSP

Features
• Land reforms and abolition of zamindari.
• Panchayati Raj institutions.
• MGNREGA reflects Article 41.

PYQ Trap
• DPSP implemented through laws, not directly enforceable.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Promote social and economic justice.
• Guide policymaking.
• Reduce inequalities.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• No legal enforcement.
• Depend on political will.

Conclusion
• DPSP provide the blueprint for a welfare state.
• They complement Fundamental Rights in achieving constitutional goals.
Polity.Fundamental Duties:
FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES

Introduction
• Fundamental Duties are moral obligations imposed on citizens to promote national discipline, unity and integrity.
• They complement Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.

Important Points
• Enshrined in Part IVA (Article 51A).
• Added by 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

PYQ Trap
• Fundamental Duties added during Emergency period (1976).

FEATURES OF FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES

Features
• Non-justiciable – not enforceable by courts.
• Apply only to citizens (not to foreigners).
• Derived from the Constitution of USSR (Soviet Union).

PYQ Trap
• Duties apply only to citizens (important elimination point).

NUMBER OF DUTIES

Important Points
• Originally 10 duties.
• 11th duty added by 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

PYQ Trap
• 11th duty relates to education of children between 6–14 years.

LIST OF IMPORTANT DUTIES

Features
• Respect Constitution, National Flag and National Anthem.
• Promote harmony and spirit of brotherhood.
• Preserve rich heritage of culture.
• Protect environment (forests, lakes, wildlife).
• Safeguard public property.
• Develop scientific temper.

PYQ Trap
• Environmental protection duty frequently asked in prelims.

NATURE OF DUTIES

Important Points
• Not legally enforceable, but can be enforced through laws.
• Courts can consider them while interpreting laws.

PYQ Trap
• Duties indirectly enforceable through legislation.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• Courts have used Fundamental Duties to interpret constitutional validity of laws.
• Environmental judgments often refer to Article 51A(g).

PYQ Trap
• Article 51A(g) → environment protection.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Promote civic responsibility and patriotism.
• Help in maintaining discipline and national unity.
• Strengthen democratic structure.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• No direct enforcement mechanism.
• Some duties are vague and open-ended.

Conclusion
• Fundamental Duties serve as ethical obligations for citizens.
• They balance rights with responsibilities in a democratic system.
Polity.President of India:
PRESIDENT OF INDIA

Introduction
• The President is the constitutional head of the State and the first citizen of India.
• All executive actions are taken in the name of the President.

Important Points
• Articles 52–78 deal with Union Executive.

PYQ Trap
• President is nominal executive, real power with Council of Ministers.

ELECTION OF PRESIDENT

Features
• Elected indirectly by Electoral College.

Important Points
• Electoral College includes:
  – Elected members of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
  – Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies
• Nominated members are not included.

PYQ Trap
• MLAs of Union Territories (Delhi & Puducherry) also participate.

ELECTION METHOD

Features
• Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote.
• Secret ballot.

PYQ Trap
• Value of vote differs for MPs and MLAs.

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Citizen of India.
• Minimum age 35 years.
• Qualified for Lok Sabha membership.

TENURE

Features
• 5 years term.
• Eligible for re-election.

REMOVAL (IMPEACHMENT)

Features
• Can be removed for violation of Constitution.

Important Points
• Impeachment initiated by either House of Parliament.

PYQ Trap
• Impeachment is quasi-judicial in nature.

EXECUTIVE POWERS

Features
• Appoints Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.
• Appoints Governors, Judges, CAG, Election Commissioners.

PYQ Trap
• Appointments are made on advice of Council of Ministers.

LEGISLATIVE POWERS

Features
• Summons and prorogues Parliament.
• Addresses Parliament.
• Assent to bills.

Important Points
• Can return ordinary bill for reconsideration.

PYQ Trap
• Cannot return Money Bill.

ORDINANCE POWER

Features
• Article 123 → Can promulgate ordinance when Parliament not in session.

PYQ Trap
• Ordinance has same force as law.

JUDICIAL POWERS

Features
• Article 72 → Power to grant pardon, reprieve, respite, remission, commutation.

PYQ Trap
• President can pardon death sentence.

FINANCIAL POWERS

Features
• Money Bill can be introduced only with President’s recommendation.
• Annual Budget presented in name of President.

EMERGENCY POWERS

Features
• National Emergency (Article 352)
• State Emergency (Article 356)
• Financial Emergency (Article 360)

PYQ Trap
• President acts on advice of Cabinet in emergency.

VETO POWERS

Features
• Absolute veto → Reject bill.
• Suspensive veto → Return bill.
• Pocket veto → No action.

PYQ Trap
• Pocket veto used in India (e.g., Zail Singh case).

DISCRETIONARY POWERS

Important Points
• Limited discretionary powers.
• Mainly in appointment of PM when no clear majority.

PYQ Trap
• President usually bound by advice of Council of Ministers (Article 74).

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• 42nd Amendment → Made advice binding.
• 44th Amendment → President can ask reconsideration once.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures continuity of government.
• Symbol of unity and integrity of nation.

Conclusion
• The President is the nominal executive with vast constitutional powers.
• Functions largely on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.
Polity.Vice President:
VICE-PRESIDENT OF INDIA

Introduction
• The Vice-President is the second highest constitutional office in India.
• He acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

Important Points
• Articles 63–71 deal with Vice-President.

PYQ Trap
• Vice-President is not part of executive like President.

ELECTION OF VICE-PRESIDENT

Features
• Elected indirectly.

Important Points
• Electoral College includes:
  – Members of both Houses of Parliament (elected + nominated)

PYQ Trap
• Unlike President, nominated members also vote.

ELECTION METHOD

Features
• Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote.
• Secret ballot.

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Citizen of India.
• Minimum age 35 years.
• Qualified for Rajya Sabha membership.

PYQ Trap
• Qualification linked to Rajya Sabha, not Lok Sabha.

TENURE

Features
• Term of 5 years.

Important Points
• Eligible for re-election.

REMOVAL

Features
• Removed by resolution of Rajya Sabha.

Important Points
• Requires majority in Rajya Sabha and agreement of Lok Sabha.

PYQ Trap
• No formal impeachment like President.

FUNCTIONS OF VICE-PRESIDENT

LEGISLATIVE ROLE

Features
• Ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha.

Important Points
• Presides over proceedings of Rajya Sabha.
• Maintains order and discipline.

PYQ Trap
• Does not vote in first instance, only casting vote in case of tie.

EXECUTIVE ROLE

Features
• Acts as President in absence of President.

Important Points
• Performs functions during vacancy or absence of President.

PYQ Trap
• Acts as President, not becomes President.

RELATION WITH PRESIDENT

Important Points
• Acts as substitute when President unable to discharge duties.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures continuity in executive.
• Maintains functioning of Rajya Sabha.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• Limited executive powers.
• Mainly legislative role.

Conclusion
• The Vice-President plays a dual role as presiding officer of Rajya Sabha and as a standby executive authority.
• Though limited in powers, the office is crucial for constitutional continuity.
Polity.Prime Minister:
PRIME MINISTER

Introduction
• The Prime Minister is the real executive authority in India.
• He is the head of the Council of Ministers and the leader of the government.

Important Points
• Articles 74 and 75 deal with Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.

PYQ Trap
• Real executive = Prime Minister, not President.

APPOINTMENT OF PRIME MINISTER

Features
• Appointed by the President.

Important Points
• Leader of majority party in Lok Sabha is appointed.
• In case of no clear majority → President exercises discretion.

PYQ Trap
• PM must prove majority in Lok Sabha.

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Must be a member of Parliament.

Important Points
• If not a member → must become MP within 6 months.

PYQ Trap
• PM can be from Rajya Sabha also.

POSITION AND ROLE

Features
• Head of government.
• Leader of Lok Sabha (usually).
• Principal advisor to President.

PYQ Trap
• PM is the pivot of entire political system.

POWERS AND FUNCTIONS

EXECUTIVE POWERS

Features
• Selects and appoints Council of Ministers.
• Allocates portfolios.
• Can recommend removal of ministers.

PYQ Trap
• Ministers hold office at pleasure of President but actually controlled by PM.

LEGISLATIVE POWERS

Features
• Leader of House.
• Decides government agenda in Parliament.
• Advises President on summoning and dissolution.

PYQ Trap
• PM plays key role in legislative process.

ADMINISTRATIVE POWERS

Features
• Coordinates work of ministries.
• Chairs Cabinet meetings.

FINANCIAL POWERS

Features
• Plays key role in budget formulation through Cabinet.

DIPLOMATIC POWERS

Features
• Represents India internationally.
• Shapes foreign policy.

RELATION WITH PRESIDENT

Important Points
• Acts as link between President and Council of Ministers.
• Advises President on all matters.

PYQ Trap
• President bound by advice of PM (Article 74).

COUNCIL OF MINISTERS

Features
• Collective responsibility to Lok Sabha.

PYQ Trap
• Collective responsibility = core feature of parliamentary system.

TENURE OF PRIME MINISTER

Features
• No fixed tenure.
• Continues as long as majority support exists.

REMOVAL

Features
• Removed when loses majority in Lok Sabha.

PYQ Trap
• No impeachment for PM.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Central figure in administration.
• Ensures stability and policy direction.

Conclusion
• The Prime Minister is the real centre of power in Indian polity.
• The entire governance system revolves around the office of the Prime Minister.
Polity.Council of Ministers:
COUNCIL OF MINISTERS

Introduction
• The Council of Ministers (CoM) is the real executive body that exercises actual authority in India.
• It functions under the leadership of the Prime Minister.

Important Points
• Articles 74 and 75 deal with Council of Ministers.

PYQ Trap
• Real executive = Council of Ministers, not President.

COMPOSITION OF COUNCIL OF MINISTERS

Features
• Cabinet Ministers
• Ministers of State (with or without independent charge)
• Deputy Ministers

PYQ Trap
• Constitution does not classify ministers into categories.

APPOINTMENT

Features
• Appointed by the President on advice of Prime Minister.

Important Points
• Prime Minister selects ministers.

PYQ Trap
• President has no independent choice in appointment.

COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY

Features
• Council of Ministers collectively responsible to Lok Sabha.

Important Points
• All ministers stand or fall together.

PYQ Trap
• Collective responsibility is core feature of parliamentary system.

INDIVIDUAL RESPONSIBILITY

Features
• Ministers hold office during pleasure of President.

Important Points
• In practice → controlled by Prime Minister.

PYQ Trap
• Pleasure of President = actually pleasure of PM.

TENURE

Features
• No fixed tenure.

Important Points
• Continues as long as majority in Lok Sabha exists.

LIMIT ON SIZE OF MINISTRY

Features
• 91st Amendment Act (2003).

Important Points
• Maximum size = 15% of Lok Sabha strength.

PYQ Trap
• Applies to both Union and State governments.

CABINET

Features
• Inner core of Council of Ministers.

Important Points
• Takes major policy decisions.

PYQ Trap
• Cabinet is not mentioned in original Constitution.

CABINET COMMITTEES

Features
• Smaller groups for efficient decision-making.

ROLE AND FUNCTIONS

EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONS

Features
• Formulation and execution of policies.

LEGISLATIVE FUNCTIONS

Features
• Introduces bills and controls legislative agenda.

FINANCIAL FUNCTIONS

Features
• Prepares budget.

RELATION WITH PRESIDENT

Important Points
• President acts on advice of Council of Ministers.

PYQ Trap
• Advice binding after 42nd Amendment.

IMPORTANT AMENDMENTS

Important Points
• 42nd Amendment → Made advice binding.
• 44th Amendment → President can ask reconsideration once.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Core decision-making body.
• Ensures coordination in administration.

Conclusion
• The Council of Ministers is the real executive authority in India.
• It ensures effective governance under the parliamentary system.
Polity.Parliament:
PARLIAMENT

Introduction
• Parliament is the supreme legislative body of India.
• It consists of the President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

Important Points
• Articles 79–122 deal with Parliament.

PYQ Trap
• President is an integral part of Parliament.

COMPOSITION OF PARLIAMENT

Features
• President
• Lok Sabha (House of People)
• Rajya Sabha (Council of States)

PYQ Trap
• Parliament ≠ only Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

LOK SABHA

Features
• Lower House, directly elected.

Important Points
• Maximum strength → 552.
• Present strength → 543 elected members.
• Tenure → 5 years (can be dissolved earlier).

PYQ Trap
• Only Lok Sabha can be dissolved.

RAJYA SABHA

Features
• Upper House, permanent body.

Important Points
• Maximum strength → 250.
• 1/3rd members retire every 2 years.
• Tenure of members → 6 years.

PYQ Trap
• Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved.

SPEAKER OF LOK SABHA

Features
• Presiding officer of Lok Sabha.

Important Points
• Decides Money Bill status.
• Maintains order in House.

PYQ Trap
• Speaker’s decision on Money Bill is final.

LEGISLATIVE PROCEDURE

Features
• Bills can be introduced in either House.

Important Points
• Ordinary Bill → Both Houses must pass.
• Joint sitting possible in case of deadlock.

PYQ Trap
• Joint sitting only for Ordinary Bills.

MONEY BILL

Features
• Article 110 defines Money Bill.

Important Points
• Can be introduced only in Lok Sabha.
• Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes.

PYQ Trap
• Rajya Sabha cannot reject Money Bill.

FINANCIAL POWERS

Features
• Budget presented annually.

Important Points
• Demand for grants voted only by Lok Sabha.

PYQ Trap
• Rajya Sabha has no voting power on grants.

CONTROL OVER EXECUTIVE

Features
• Question Hour, Zero Hour.
• No-confidence motion.

PYQ Trap
• No-confidence motion only in Lok Sabha.

SPECIAL POWERS OF RAJYA SABHA

Features
• Article 249 → Can allow Parliament to legislate on State List.
• Article 312 → Creation of All India Services.

PYQ Trap
• Rajya Sabha has special federal powers.

PARLIAMENTARY PRIVILEGES

Features
• Freedom of speech in Parliament.
• Immunity from court proceedings.

PYQ Trap
• Privileges not fully codified.

IMPORTANT ARTICLES

Important Points
• Article 79 → Constitution of Parliament.
• Article 85 → Sessions of Parliament.
• Article 110 → Money Bill.
• Article 111 → Assent to Bills.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Law-making body of India.
• Controls executive.
• Represents people and states.

Conclusion
• Parliament is the cornerstone of Indian democracy.
• It ensures accountability, representation and law-making.
Polity.Supreme Court:
SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

Introduction
• The Supreme Court is the highest judicial authority in India.
• It is the guardian of the Constitution and protector of Fundamental Rights.

Important Points
• Established under Article 124.

PYQ Trap
• Supreme Court = guardian of Constitution (frequently asked).

COMPOSITION OF SUPREME COURT

Features
• Chief Justice of India + other judges.

Important Points
• Strength decided by Parliament.

PYQ Trap
• Number of judges is not fixed in Constitution.

APPOINTMENT OF JUDGES

Features
• Appointed by the President.

Important Points
• Based on Collegium System (judicial evolution).

PYQ Trap
• Collegium not mentioned in Constitution.

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Citizen of India.
• Judge of High Court for 5 years OR
• Advocate of High Court for 10 years OR
• Distinguished jurist.

TENURE

Features
• Judges hold office till 65 years of age.

REMOVAL OF JUDGES

Features
• Removed by impeachment by Parliament.

Important Points
• Grounds → proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

PYQ Trap
• Removal requires special majority in both Houses.

JURISDICTION OF SUPREME COURT

ORIGINAL JURISDICTION

Features
• Article 131 → Centre-State disputes.

APPELLATE JURISDICTION

Features
• Appeals from High Courts in civil, criminal and constitutional cases.

WRIT JURISDICTION

Features
• Article 32 → Enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

PYQ Trap
• Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right.

ADVISORY JURISDICTION

Features
• Article 143 → President can seek advice.

PYQ Trap
• Advice is not binding on President.

JUDICIAL REVIEW

Features
• Power to examine constitutionality of laws.

PYQ Trap
• Judicial Review = Basic Structure.

JUDICIAL ACTIVISM AND PIL

Features
• Public Interest Litigation allows access to justice.

Important Points
• Relaxation of locus standi.

PYQ Trap
• PIL expanded scope of Article 21.

IMPORTANT DOCTRINES

Features
• Basic Structure Doctrine.
• Doctrine of Judicial Review.

PYQ Trap
• Basic Structure evolved in Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• Kesavananda Bharati → Basic Structure.
• Maneka Gandhi → Expanded Article 21.
• NJAC Case (2015) → Collegium upheld.

PYQ Trap
• NJAC declared unconstitutional.

INDEPENDENCE OF JUDICIARY

Features
• Security of tenure.
• Fixed service conditions.
• Separation from executive.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Protects Fundamental Rights.
• Ensures constitutional supremacy.
• Maintains federal balance.

Conclusion
• The Supreme Court plays a vital role in safeguarding democracy.
• It ensures rule of law and constitutional governance.
Polity.High Court:
HIGH COURT

Introduction
• The High Court is the highest judicial authority at the State level.
• It acts as a guardian of Fundamental Rights within its territorial jurisdiction.

Important Points
• Articles 214–231 deal with High Courts.

PYQ Trap
• Every State has a High Court, but one High Court can serve multiple States.

COMPOSITION OF HIGH COURT

Features
• Chief Justice and other judges.

Important Points
• Number of judges determined by the President.

PYQ Trap
• Strength not fixed in Constitution.

APPOINTMENT OF JUDGES

Features
• Appointed by the President.

Important Points
• Consultation with Chief Justice of India and Governor.
• Collegium system followed (judicial evolution).

PYQ Trap
• Collegium not mentioned in Constitution.

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Citizen of India.
• At least 10 years judicial office OR advocate of High Court for 10 years.

TENURE

Features
• Judges hold office till 62 years.

PYQ Trap
• HC retirement age = 62 (SC = 65).

REMOVAL

Features
• Same procedure as Supreme Court judges.

Important Points
• Removal by Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

JURISDICTION OF HIGH COURT

ORIGINAL JURISDICTION

Features
• In certain civil and criminal matters.

WRIT JURISDICTION

Features
• Article 226 → Can issue writs.

Important Points
• Wider than Supreme Court (Article 32).

PYQ Trap
• HC can issue writs for FR and other legal rights.

APPELLATE JURISDICTION

Features
• Appeals from subordinate courts.

SUPERVISORY JURISDICTION

Features
• Article 227 → Superintendence over subordinate courts.

PYQ Trap
• Supervisory power unique feature of High Court.

COURT OF RECORD

Features
• Can punish for contempt of court.

TRANSFER OF JUDGES

Features
• President can transfer judges from one HC to another.

Important Points
• Consultation with Chief Justice of India.

INDEPENDENCE OF HIGH COURT

Features
• Security of tenure.
• Fixed service conditions.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Protects rights at State level.
• Ensures judicial control over administration.

Conclusion
• The High Court plays a vital role in maintaining rule of law at the State level.
• It acts as a bridge between Supreme Court and subordinate judiciary.
Polity.Subordinate Courts:
SUBORDINATE COURTS

Introduction
• Subordinate Courts operate below the High Courts and handle civil and criminal cases at district and local levels.
• They form the base of the judicial pyramid in India.

Important Points
• Articles 233–237 deal with Subordinate Courts.

PYQ Trap
• Subordinate Courts are under control of High Courts.

STRUCTURE OF SUBORDINATE COURTS

Features
• District Courts
• Sessions Courts (criminal)
• Civil Courts (District Judge, Civil Judge)
• Magistrate Courts

PYQ Trap
• District Judge is highest judicial authority at district level.

APPOINTMENT OF DISTRICT JUDGES

Features
• Appointed by Governor.

Important Points
• Consultation with High Court.

PYQ Trap
• High Court plays key role in appointment.

APPOINTMENT OF OTHER JUDGES

Features
• Appointed by Governor as per rules.

CONTROL OF HIGH COURT

Features
• Article 235 → High Court exercises control over subordinate judiciary.

Important Points
• Includes posting, promotion and discipline.

PYQ Trap
• Control lies with High Court, not State Government.

SEPARATION OF JUDICIARY

Features
• Article 50 → Separation of judiciary from executive.

Important Points
• Ensures independence of judiciary.

JURISDICTION

Features
• Civil and criminal jurisdiction at local level.

IMPORTANT ROLES

Features
• Handling majority of litigation.
• Providing access to justice at grassroots level.

COURTS OF RECORD

Features
• Subordinate courts are not courts of record.

PYQ Trap
• Only Supreme Court and High Courts are courts of record.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures justice delivery at grassroots.
• Reduces burden on higher judiciary.

Conclusion
• Subordinate Courts are essential for effective administration of justice.
• They strengthen the judicial system by ensuring accessibility and efficiency.
Polity.Governor:
GOVERNOR

Introduction
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the State.
• He acts as the nominal executive and representative of the President in the State.

Important Points
• Articles 153–167 deal with Governor.

PYQ Trap
• Governor = agent of Centre in State.

APPOINTMENT OF GOVERNOR

Features
• Appointed by the President.

Important Points
• Not elected.
• Holds office at pleasure of President.

PYQ Trap
• No fixed tenure guarantee (though nominally 5 years).

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Citizen of India.
• Minimum age 35 years.

Important Points
• Cannot be member of Parliament or State Legislature.

TENURE

Features
• Term of 5 years.

PYQ Trap
• Can be removed anytime by President.

EXECUTIVE POWERS

Features
• Appoints Chief Minister.
• Appoints Council of Ministers.
• Appoints Advocate General and State officials.

PYQ Trap
• Ministers hold office at pleasure of Governor (but actually CM controlled).

LEGISLATIVE POWERS

Features
• Summons and prorogues State Legislature.
• Assent to bills.

Important Points
• Can reserve bill for President.

PYQ Trap
• Governor can reserve bill for President (important power).

ORDINANCE POWER

Features
• Article 213 → Can issue ordinance when legislature not in session.

PYQ Trap
• Ordinance has same force as law.

JUDICIAL POWERS

Features
• Can grant pardons, reprieves etc.

Important Points
• Cannot pardon death sentence (unlike President).

PYQ Trap
• Governor cannot pardon death sentence.

DISCRETIONARY POWERS

Features
• Appointment of CM when no clear majority.
• Sending report for President’s Rule.

PYQ Trap
• Discretionary powers not explicitly defined in Constitution.

ROLE IN PRESIDENT’S RULE

Features
• Article 356 → Governor reports failure of constitutional machinery.

PYQ Trap
• Governor’s report basis for President’s Rule.

RELATION WITH CHIEF MINISTER

Important Points
• CM is real executive at State level.
• Governor acts on advice of Council of Ministers.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• SR Bommai Case (1994) → Limited misuse of Article 356.
• Nabam Rebia Case (2016) → Limits on Governor’s discretionary powers.

PYQ Trap
• Governor’s power not absolute.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures constitutional governance in State.
• Acts as link between Centre and State.

Conclusion
• The Governor is a constitutional head with limited real powers.
• Functions largely on advice of the Council of Ministers, with some discretionary powers.
Polity.Centre-State Relations:
CENTRE–STATE RELATIONS

Introduction
• Centre–State relations define the distribution of powers between the Union and the States.
• India follows a federal system with a strong unitary bias.

Important Points
• Part XI (Articles 245–263) deals with Centre–State relations.

PYQ Trap
• India is federal in structure but unitary in spirit.

LEGISLATIVE RELATIONS

Features
• Distribution of legislative powers through Seventh Schedule.

Important Points
• Union List (List I) → Centre
• State List (List II) → States
• Concurrent List (List III) → Both

PYQ Trap
• Residuary powers lie with Centre (unlike USA).

SPECIAL PROVISIONS

Features
• Article 249 → Parliament can legislate on State List in national interest (Rajya Sabha resolution).
• Article 250 → During Emergency.
• Article 252 → With consent of States.
• Article 253 → For international agreements.

PYQ Trap
• Article 249 requires Rajya Sabha resolution (not Lok Sabha).

ADMINISTRATIVE RELATIONS

Features
• Centre can give directions to States.

Important Points
• Article 256 → State must comply with Union laws.
• Article 257 → Centre control over States.

PYQ Trap
• Failure to comply can lead to Article 356.

FINANCIAL RELATIONS

Features
• Distribution of taxes between Centre and States.

Important Points
• Articles 268–293 deal with financial relations.
• Finance Commission (Article 280) recommends distribution.

PYQ Trap
• Finance Commission is constitutional body.

INTER-STATE RELATIONS

Features
• Article 262 → Inter-State water disputes.
• Article 263 → Inter-State Council.

PYQ Trap
• Inter-State Council established under Article 263.

EMERGENCY PROVISIONS AND FEDERALISM

Features
• Centre becomes dominant during Emergency.

Important Points
• Article 352 → National Emergency.
• Article 356 → President’s Rule.

PYQ Trap
• Federal system becomes unitary during emergency.

ROLE OF GOVERNOR

Important Points
• Acts as link between Centre and State.
• Reports constitutional breakdown.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• SR Bommai Case (1994) → Federalism part of Basic Structure.

PYQ Trap
• Federalism is part of Basic Structure.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Maintains unity and integrity.
• Balances national and regional interests.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• Strong Centre may affect State autonomy.

Conclusion
• Centre–State relations ensure cooperative federalism.
• They maintain balance between unity and diversity in India.
Polity.Emergency Provisions:
EMERGENCY PROVISIONS

Introduction
• Emergency provisions enable the Central government to assume extraordinary powers to deal with abnormal situations.
• They convert the federal structure into a unitary one during crisis.

Important Points
• Part XVIII (Articles 352–360) deals with Emergency.

PYQ Trap
• Emergency provisions borrowed from German Constitution.

TYPES OF EMERGENCY

Features
• National Emergency (Article 352)
• State Emergency / President’s Rule (Article 356)
• Financial Emergency (Article 360)

PYQ Trap
• Three types of emergencies – frequently asked.

NATIONAL EMERGENCY (ARTICLE 352)

Features
• Declared on grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion.

Important Points
• Earlier term “internal disturbance” replaced by “armed rebellion” (44th Amendment).

PYQ Trap
• Armed rebellion = current ground.

APPROVAL AND DURATION

Features
• Must be approved by Parliament within 1 month.

Important Points
• Requires special majority.
• Continues for 6 months and can be extended.

PYQ Trap
• Special majority required (not simple majority).

EFFECTS OF NATIONAL EMERGENCY

Features
• Centre becomes powerful.
• Parliament can legislate on State List.

Important Points
• Fundamental Rights under Article 19 automatically suspended.
• Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended.

PYQ Trap
• Article 20 & 21 always protected.

STATE EMERGENCY (ARTICLE 356)

Features
• Declared on failure of constitutional machinery in State.

Important Points
• Based on Governor’s report.
• State government dismissed.

PYQ Trap
• Maximum duration → 3 years (with conditions).

EFFECTS OF PRESIDENT’S RULE

Features
• Parliament assumes legislative powers of State.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENT

Important Points
• SR Bommai Case (1994) → Limited misuse of Article 356.

PYQ Trap
• Judicial review applicable on President’s Rule.

FINANCIAL EMERGENCY (ARTICLE 360)

Features
• Declared when financial stability threatened.

Important Points
• Salaries of officials may be reduced.

PYQ Trap
• Never declared in India till now.

REVOCATION OF EMERGENCY

Features
• Can be revoked by President anytime.

Important Points
• Lok Sabha can pass resolution to revoke.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures stability during crisis.
• Protects national integrity.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• Potential misuse (historically during 1975 Emergency).

Conclusion
• Emergency provisions are essential but require careful use.
• Safeguards added by 44th Amendment ensure protection of democracy.
Polity.Amendment of Constitution:
AMENDMENT OF CONSTITUTION

Introduction
• The Constitution provides a mechanism for its own amendment to adapt to changing needs.
• It balances rigidity and flexibility.

Important Points
• Article 368 deals with amendment procedure.

PYQ Trap
• Amendment procedure not entirely rigid or flexible.

TYPES OF AMENDMENTS

Features
• By Simple Majority
• By Special Majority
• By Special Majority + Ratification by States

PYQ Trap
• Not all amendments under Article 368.

SIMPLE MAJORITY

Features
• Outside Article 368.

Important Points
• Used for matters like formation of new states, citizenship, etc.

PYQ Trap
• Simple majority ≠ constitutional amendment under Article 368.

SPECIAL MAJORITY

Features
• Majority of total membership + 2/3rd of members present and voting.

Important Points
• Used for most constitutional amendments.

SPECIAL MAJORITY WITH STATE RATIFICATION

Features
• Requires approval by half of State Legislatures.

Important Points
• Used for federal provisions.

PYQ Trap
• Federal provisions need State ratification.

PROCEDURE OF AMENDMENT

Features
• Bill introduced in either House of Parliament.

Important Points
• No joint sitting allowed.
• President must give assent (cannot veto).

PYQ Trap
• President cannot return amendment bill.

LIMITATIONS ON AMENDMENT

Features
• Parliament cannot amend Basic Structure.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• Shankari Prasad (1951) → Amendment valid.
• Golaknath (1967) → FR cannot be amended.
• Kesavananda Bharati (1973) → Basic Structure doctrine.

PYQ Trap
• Kesavananda case = most important.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Allows Constitution to evolve.
• Maintains balance between change and stability.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• Possibility of misuse.
• Judicial intervention required.

Conclusion
• The amendment process ensures adaptability of the Constitution.
• It is subject to judicial limitations to protect its core structure.
Polity.Basic Structure Doctrine:
BASIC STRUCTURE DOCTRINE

Introduction
• The Basic Structure Doctrine states that Parliament cannot alter the basic structure or core framework of the Constitution.
• It acts as a limitation on the amending power of Parliament.

Important Points
• Evolved through judicial interpretation.

PYQ Trap
• Basic Structure not mentioned in Constitution.

ORIGIN OF DOCTRINE

Features
• Developed in Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).

Important Points
• Supreme Court held that Article 368 does not give unlimited power to amend.

PYQ Trap
• Kesavananda case = origin of Basic Structure.

EVOLUTION THROUGH CASE LAWS

Important Points
• Shankari Prasad (1951) → Parliament can amend FR.
• Golaknath (1967) → FR cannot be amended.
• Kesavananda Bharati (1973) → Basic Structure introduced.
• Minerva Mills (1980) → Balance between FR and DPSP part of Basic Structure.

PYQ Trap
• Minerva Mills reinforced Basic Structure.

ELEMENTS OF BASIC STRUCTURE

Features
• Supremacy of Constitution.
• Rule of Law.
• Separation of Powers.
• Judicial Review.
• Federalism.
• Secularism.
• Parliamentary System.
• Unity and Integrity of Nation.

PYQ Trap
• No fixed list of Basic Structure elements.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Prevents misuse of amendment power.
• Protects democratic framework.
• Ensures constitutional supremacy.

LIMITATIONS ON PARLIAMENT

Features
• Parliament cannot destroy or alter core principles.

PYQ Trap
• Amendment allowed but not destruction.

RELATION WITH ARTICLE 368

Important Points
• Article 368 gives power to amend.
• Basic Structure restricts that power.

SIGNIFICANCE IN GOVERNANCE

Important Points
• Acts as safeguard against authoritarianism.
• Maintains balance of power.

Conclusion
• The Basic Structure Doctrine is a judicial innovation that preserves the essence of the Constitution.
• It ensures continuity of democratic governance in India.
Polity.Election Commission:
ELECTION COMMISSION OF INDIA

Introduction
• The Election Commission of India (ECI) is an autonomous constitutional body responsible for administering elections in India.
• It ensures free and fair elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and offices of President and Vice-President.

Important Points
• Article 324 deals with Election Commission.

PYQ Trap
• ECI conducts elections for President, Vice-President, Parliament and State Legislatures (not local bodies).

COMPOSITION OF ELECTION COMMISSION

Features
• Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) + Election Commissioners.

Important Points
• Number of Election Commissioners decided by President.

PYQ Trap
• Constitution does not fix number of members.

APPOINTMENT

Features
• Appointed by the President.

Important Points
• No specific qualification mentioned in Constitution.

TENURE

Features
• 6 years or up to age of 65 years (whichever earlier).

PYQ Trap
• Same tenure rule for all Election Commissioners.

REMOVAL

Features
• CEC → Removed like Supreme Court judge.
• Other ECs → Removed by President on recommendation of CEC.

PYQ Trap
• CEC enjoys stronger protection than other ECs.

POWERS AND FUNCTIONS

Features
• Conducts elections to Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and State Legislatures.
• Supervises electoral rolls.
• Recognizes political parties and allots symbols.

PYQ Trap
• Symbol allotment is an important function.

MODEL CODE OF CONDUCT

Features
• Ensures ethical conduct during elections.

Important Points
• Not legally binding but enforced strictly.

PYQ Trap
• MCC not a law.

INDEPENDENCE OF ECI

Features
• Security of tenure.
• Fixed service conditions.

Important Points
• Removal procedure safeguards independence.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• Dependent on government for staff.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures democratic legitimacy.
• Maintains electoral integrity.

Conclusion
• The Election Commission is a cornerstone of Indian democracy.
• It ensures free, fair and transparent elections across the country.
Polity.Finance Commission:
FINANCE COMMISSION

Introduction
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body that recommends the distribution of financial resources between the Centre and the States.
• It plays a key role in maintaining fiscal federalism.

Important Points
• Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission.

PYQ Trap
• Finance Commission is a constitutional body (not statutory).

COMPOSITION

Features
• Chairman + four other members.

Important Points
• Appointed by the President.

PYQ Trap
• Qualifications determined by Parliament, not Constitution.

TENURE

Features
• Appointed every 5 years or earlier if required.

FUNCTIONS OF FINANCE COMMISSION

Features
• Recommend distribution of net proceeds of taxes between Centre and States.
• Recommend allocation among States.
• Suggest principles governing grants-in-aid.

PYQ Trap
• Tax devolution is primary function.

ADVISORY ROLE

Features
• Recommendations are advisory in nature.

PYQ Trap
• Not binding on government.

FINANCE COMMISSION VS NITI AAYOG

Important Points
• Finance Commission → Constitutional, deals with tax distribution.
• NITI Aayog → Non-constitutional, policy advisory body.

PYQ Trap
• NITI Aayog does not replace Finance Commission.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures financial balance.
• Promotes cooperative federalism.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• Advisory nature reduces binding power.

Conclusion
• Finance Commission is essential for fiscal stability and Centre–State relations.
• It ensures equitable distribution of financial resources in India.
